Validating Every Route

validate({ ... }) applied per-route, right where each route is defined.

Everything so far — schemas, the validate factory, coercion — comes together at the one place a schema actually gets attached to a request: the route definition itself.

// Figure 3.7: applying validation per-route (src/routes/ticket.routes.js, excerpt)
router.get('/', validate({ query: listTicketsQuerySchema }), ticketController.getAllTickets);
router.post('/', validate({ body: createTicketSchema }), ticketController.createTicket);

router.get('/:id', validate({ params: ticketIdParamSchema }), ticketController.getTicketById);
router.patch(
  '/:id',
  validate({ params: ticketIdParamSchema, body: updateTicketSchema }),
  ticketController.updateTicket,
);

validate({ ... }) sits in the middle of router.get(path, ...)'s argument list, between the path and the controller — an ordinary Express middleware position (Lesson 1's routing topic). Express runs middleware in the order they're listed, so by the time ticketController.createTicket runs, the request has already passed validate({ body: createTicketSchema }) — if it hadn't, validate would have called next(new ApiError(...)) instead of next(), and Express would have skipped straight past the controller to the centralized error handler, exactly like asyncHandler does for a rejected Promise.

Notice PATCH /:id passes two schemas at once — { params: ticketIdParamSchema, body: updateTicketSchema } — since that one route needs both the URL's :id and the request body checked before either is trusted. That's exactly why validate.js loops over params/query/body (Figure 3.5) instead of only ever handling one part of the request: a single call covers whatever combination a route actually needs, nothing more.

With this in place, every controller function this project writes from here on can read req.params, req.query, and req.body and trust their shape completely — the manual if (!subject || ...) checks and Number.isNaN guards from Lessons 1 and 2 (first slide, this topic) are gone from ticket.controller.js for good.
